criteria.justification: The response explicitly notes that "The earlier paused launch is a warning—not proof—that good mapping accuracy is insufficient," recognizing that past on-paper performance didn't translate to value.
The candidate successfully avoids the sunk cost fallacy by stating that the team's past year of investment "should influence how we transition, not determine what success means."

The response acknowledges that "Until outcome data exists, launch readiness is unproven" and proposes a concrete interim plan to make ground-truth collection a dependency and run a bounded validation pilot.

The candidate recognizes this by noting that "Another year of optimization against [the old metric] would not resolve that gap" and that evaluating the new metric will help direct "engineering effort" toward errors that actually affect customers.

The response offers a very concrete recommendation: "make accuracy against the customer-relevant risk-exposure number the primary launch criterion, with mapping accuracy retained as a diagnostic and regression guardrail."
